questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I could go there with three of my friends on exchange

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think the student presentation and the old fashion way of doing school with a teacher telling a lot, and no interacting, is a but outdated, and it wasn't really a great experience. But kind people and very easy to get in touch with coordinaters.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I had a bit trouble with the information, and i was late on some deadlines which led to them rejecting me, and i had to sweettalk and send a lot of emails for them to enroll me in the university in Prague.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was fine, an introduction, chill not much, science get introduction one week after the registration to the courses for the whole university, so it was very hard finding courses outside science faq, which had room for more students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: niente

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used the website called Erasmus In Prague, bit expensive, but we had a place big enough for all four in the city center, it was worth it because the student dorms and other usual accomodation is outside the center, and it sounds really annoying to live in a boring neighborhood and have to use the tram for everything.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Its good, its more expensive, prague city center is expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As I said, it was a problem that the introduction for science was a week after the rest of the university, that means everyone could enroll in courses, and then science could try to find courses with room for one or two more. note: science courses are easily available for science, but if you want to have courses on another faq this is really a problem.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You will get to know their system sys, and everything happens there. Not much to tell, a bit outdated and difficult to use.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Sending mails back and forth

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: it eventually happened, but it was a battle especially for the ones i really wanted. One particularly I had to attend up to three times before I could be enrolled in the course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I dont actually know what you should do to prevent this, maybe try as soon as possible to enroll for courses you want and write to professors

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was fine, i was not on exchange for an academic reward, but merely trying different things and enjoy the time.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I got almost only a's and I had no physic course, so every course was the first time i tried that academic branch, and i could easily take part and get follow along

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: its these student presentations which are an old fashioned way, and its not that interacting, and very much a professor showing off

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester
